actual_scope: Kernel-check (Lean 4, Mathlib) the binding from an exact PRICEKIT invoice to a word's kappa. Generic: for any invoice cs (coefficients c_r, ranks r >= 1), F cs t = sum c_r r^(1-t); kernel-checked piece chains give lo <= kroot cs <= hi, F(kroot cs) = 0 and every root of F on [0, inf) in (lo, hi) (CertKit.kroot_bracket). Per word: a kernel-replayed trace of the word file, its invoice proved equal to PRICEKIT's (fold histograms), and the headline Cert<N>.certified : Legal (pub caller7113) tr AND Rows AND Word caller7113 (exec tr) AND lo <= kword AND kword <= hi with no hypotheses, where kword = sSup of kappa in [0,1) at which the word's Valid inequality holds. Done for two words under the #7113 caller: t7669 (#7669's word replayed; kword in [.00372142604386, .00372142604387]) and w_s4 (kword in [.00366673434589, .00366673434590]); the caller block is derived in the kernel from the #7113 caller file. A tool (certkit.py) emits the certificate for another word in one command. No kappa claim.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one uncovered interface implication with caller and certificate bindings; this package adds a reusable price-to-kernel binding (generic invoice bracket, trace-to-invoice link, row certificate, caller derivation) and instantiates it on two words, so the scope is wider than one implication. Recorded as changed.
bottleneck_link: Side result (verification tooling). A word's kappa is usually checked by Python pricers only; this turns the PRICEKIT value of a word under the #7113 caller into a kernel-checked statement about the word file itself (legal trace, correct rows, kappa to 10 significant digits), so conditional kappa claims of that shape can carry a Lean certificate.
stop_rule: Ship only if every Check.lean headline prints axioms within {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorry/native_decide/axiom/extern appears in the sources, the two certified headlines have no hypotheses, the regenerated data modules match their sha256 pins, and the Python side regenerates the bracket modules byte-identical from PRICEKIT; otherwise report the failing check.
evidence: verify.py (stdlib, run in CI, about 30 s) checks file pins, token bans outside comments, module set, topological order and All.lean closure (regenerated modules through their pinned imports), declared Check.lean names, the two headline statements, CHECK-axioms.txt, toolchain and Mathlib pins; it reprices both words with tools/pricekit.py, re-checks the piece certificates exactly and regenerates Cert<N>Tab/Part*/Num and the Cert<N> link modules byte-identical, and the caller modules from the caller file. verify.sh additionally regenerates the 340 large data modules (tools/regen.py, byte-identical to REGEN.json) and runs lean/check.sh (sequential guarded build of the 703-module closure plus #print axioms on 34 names; output in CHECK-axioms.txt). The trace data the kernel replays (event chunks, frame masks, checkpoints) is regenerated from the shipped word files by tools/regen.py, so the replayed trace is the word file.
